newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 16.

text.p: THE DOMINION

The National Party has announced a negotiating team designed to build bridges to influential Maori elements within NZ First. The team includes new list MP Georgina te Heuheu, a Maori and Treaty Negotiations Minister Doug Graham. NZ First leader Winston Peters said his party was committed to negotiating a coalition with Labour or National if possible. Negotiations would probably get underway next week, Peters said. Page 1.
The uncertain election result failed to dampen the sharemarket - it raced to the highest level in two and a half years, easily breaking through the 2,300 mark on Tuesday. Page 1.

Speculation on post-prime minsterial jobs for Jim Bolger offered up the high commissioner post in London as an option. Bolger is not expected to lead National into the 1999 election, regardless of whether National remains in power. Page 2.

Caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger came under fire in yesterday's National caucus meeting for his shortcomings in fronting National's campaign. Among Bolger's trip-ups on the campaign trail was a failure to perform strongly in the first big television leaders' debate. Page 2.
NZ First leader Winston Peters says his party will go into coalition with the party that offers the best deal on policy. Page 2.

David Lange has added his weight to the argument that Labour Party is on the verge of regaining government. Former prime minister Lange told a business lunch in Brisbane he expected NZ First leader Winston Peters to support Labour leader Helen Clark's bid to become prime minister. Page 2.
Standard and Poor on Tuesday reaffirmed New Zealand's credit rating and said it did not expect economic policy changes after the election to impair the country's credit standing. Page 2.

Investors' love affair with the sharemarket continued on Tuesday with the main index smashing through the 2,300 mark to close at a new 32-month high on the back of better-than-expected inflation figures. Telecom raced to a new all-time high to close on $7.32, up 32 cents. Page 18.
Wellington department store Kirkcaldie and Stains lifted net profit more than half a million dollars to $2.23 for the year ended August 31. Page 18.
Dublin-based Independent Newspapers has increased its stake in Wilson and Horton this week to 53.73 percent through its offer for cash or convertible notes. Page 18.

International investors' voracious appetite for foreign bonds denominiated in New Zealand dollars looks set to continue despite the election and a fall in yields yesterday, according to an Australian director of the dominant lead manager in the euro-kiwi bond market. Page 18.
The first victim of Underground Fashion's $2.67 million loss for the year to July will be the company's boss, who will take a pay cut. Page 18.

Sam Kavourakis's presence in New Zealand the week before the election was "purely a coincidence" the managing director of National Mutual Fund Management (Global) group said. He was here to talk with NMFM people in the wake of National Mutual's liating on the stock exchange. The listing was the final step in National Mutual's move from demutualisation to part of a global conglomerate. Page 21.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Labour and National will be played off against each other all the way through the coalition bidding war planned by New Zealand First leader Winston Peters. Negotiations with both parties - likely to be held on alternate days - will proceed without New Zealand First offering a prefernce at any stage, he indicated on Tuesday.
-- No text received

Suggestions from National that it could consider widening the zero to two percent inflation target drew a strong response from ACT NZ on Tuesday. ACT leader Richard Prebble said he was nervous at suggestions by Finance Minister Bill Birch that loosening the inflation target could be on the negotiating table in coalition talks.
National will conduct a thorough review of its election campaign strategy following strong criticism from MPs who felt it was far too negative and confused.
Alliance will today release a "discussion paper" of issues it wants discussed with Labour and New Zealand First before it will back a centre-left coalition government.
The United Party will live on, despite losing six out of it seven MPs on election night, says United MP Peter Dunne.

Confounding both private sector and Reserve Bank forecasters, the consumers price index rose 0.6 percent in the September quarter, making 2.4 percent for the year. The numbers, much better than expected, sent wholesale interst rates sharply
lower and share prices higher.

Standard and Poor's has reaffirmed New Zealand's credit rating. "Although the outcome of the election raises the possibility of a change in government, Standard and Poor's does not expect economic policy changes that would impair the sovereign's fundamental credit standing," it said.
Women's clothing retailer Underground Fashions will shut down its shop in Queen Street, Auckland as it confronts a $2.67 million loss in the July 31 year.
Fletcher Energy is to test new technology which it hopes will turn Taranaki's Mangahewa gas prospect into a significant replacement for Maui.

Power New Zealand's main council shareholders debate the future of their holdings this week against a background of increasingly succulent offers from Mercury Energy and pressure from Power New Zealand to hold the line.
